acceptanceCriteria.given: The API and Postgres are available
acceptanceCriteria.then: The API returns the created task with an id, the submitted title, and incomplete status, and the record is persisted
acceptanceCriteria.when: A client posts a valid non-empty task title

acceptanceCriteria.then: The API returns every available task with id, title, and status in the documented JSON shape
acceptanceCriteria.when: A client requests the task list

acceptanceCriteria.given: Persisted tasks exist with more than one status
acceptanceCriteria.then: The response contains only tasks with that status
acceptanceCriteria.when: A client requests a valid status filter

acceptanceCriteria.then: The API returns success and subsequent reads show the task as complete
acceptanceCriteria.when: A client requests completion for that task

acceptanceCriteria.given: An existing task and a valid replacement title exist
acceptanceCriteria.then: The API returns success and subsequent reads show the replacement title
acceptanceCriteria.when: A client submits the edit request

acceptanceCriteria.given: A task has been created and Postgres remains available
acceptanceCriteria.then: A subsequent list or get operation returns the same task id, title, and status
acceptanceCriteria.when: Only the API process is stopped and restarted

acceptanceCriteria.given: A client submits invalid task input or an invalid status filter
acceptanceCriteria.then: It returns a stable Problem Details response with an appropriate client error status and no internal diagnostic

acceptanceCriteria.given: A client references a task that does not exist
acceptanceCriteria.then: The API returns the documented not-found Problem Details response
acceptanceCriteria.when: The client requests completion or editing

acceptanceCriteria.given: The Postgres service and its persistent volume are available
acceptanceCriteria.then: Previously persisted task data remains available
acceptanceCriteria.when: The API is restarted without recreating the database volume

acceptanceCriteria.given: A clean local Postgres database is available
acceptanceCriteria.then: The required schema is created automatically and a second startup does not fail because the schema already exists

acceptanceCriteria.given: TODO_DB_CONNECTION is configured or the documented safe local default is used
acceptanceCriteria.then: It attempts to connect using that configuration and does not expose credentials in responses or logs

acceptanceCriteria.given: Postgres is unavailable or a database operation fails
acceptanceCriteria.then: The API returns a stable sanitized Problem Details response containing no credentials, stack trace, or provider-internal detail
acceptanceCriteria.when: A client invokes an affected endpoint

acceptanceCriteria.then: The API returns the documented deletion success response and subsequent list or get operations no longer return the task; a missing task returns not-found Problem Details

acceptanceCriteria.given: A clean checkout with Docker available
acceptanceCriteria.then: Postgres becomes ready through the health check, the API connects with bounded retries, and the sequence completes reproducibly
acceptanceCriteria.when: The documented Compose startup and verification sequence is run

acceptanceCriteria.given: The project is checked out and local dependencies are available
acceptanceCriteria.then: Pure unit tests and isolated serial real-HTTP/real-Postgres integration tests execute and cover create, list, filter, complete, edit, remove, validation, not-found, durability, and dependency-failure behavior
acceptanceCriteria.when: The documented test command is run

acceptanceCriteria.then: Each operation remains cohesive in its vertical slice and no generic Controller, Service, or Repository layer has been introduced
acceptanceCriteria.when: The task operation code is inspected

acceptanceCriteria.given: Validation and dependency-failure tests are run
acceptanceCriteria.then: The payloads and logs are deterministic and redact credentials, stack traces, and provider internals
acceptanceCriteria.when: Their responses and captured logs are inspected

dataRules.description: Every task has a generated stable id, a non-empty title, and a status restricted to the documented incomplete or complete values.
dataRules.name: Task identity and fields
dataRules.rule: Every task shall have a generated stable id, a non-empty title after trimming, and a status restricted to the documented incomplete or complete values.

dataRules.description: Task mutations are persisted in Postgres; completion and editing update the existing record, while removal makes the record unavailable to subsequent reads.
dataRules.name: Persistence and deletion
dataRules.rule: Task mutations shall be persisted in Postgres; completion and editing shall update the existing record, while removal shall make the record unavailable to subsequent reads.

dataRules.description: Client-visible failure payloads and logs must not include connection credentials, stack traces, or provider-internal diagnostics.
dataRules.name: Sanitized failure data
dataRules.rule: Client-visible failure payloads and logs shall not include connection credentials, stack traces, or provider-internal diagnostics.

delivery.target: A greenfield local .NET/C# ASP.NET Core task-management Web API backed by Postgres and Docker Compose, with no frontend, identity, cloud deployment, migration, or regulated-data scope.
delivery.verificationStrategy: Run the documented Docker Compose setup, verify automatic schema initialization and API-only restart durability, then run pure unit tests and isolated serial real-HTTP/real-Postgres integration tests for all six operations and failure contracts.

functionalRequirements.statement: The API shall accept an unauthenticated JSON POST request to create a task with a non-empty title, persist the task with a generated identifier and initial incomplete status, and return the created task as stable JSON.
The API shall accept an unauthenticated JSON GET request to list tasks and return stable JSON containing each task's id, title, and status.
The API shall support filtering the task list by task status and shall return only tasks matching the requested valid status value.
The API shall accept an unauthenticated request to complete an existing task, persist its status as complete, and return the updated task as stable JSON.
The API shall accept an unauthenticated JSON request to edit an existing task title, persist the updated title, and return the updated task as stable JSON.

The API shall persist each task's id, title, and status in Postgres and shall read those records from Postgres for subsequent requests, preserving them when only the API process is stopped and restarted.
On local startup, the application shall initialize the required task schema in Postgres automatically and shall be safe to run against an already initialized schema.

The application shall obtain its Postgres connection from TODO_DB_CONNECTION, document a safe local default without committing credentials, and fail startup or requests with a sanitized diagnostic when the dependency is unavailable.

Each task operation shall expose a stable JSON success contract and stable Problem Details responses for invalid input, a missing task, and dependency failures, without credentials, stack traces, or provider-internal details.

The API shall accept an unauthenticated request to remove an existing task and shall return the documented successful deletion response; attempting to remove a missing task shall return the documented Problem Details response.

interfaces.description: Unauthenticated local HTTP clients use JSON endpoints for create, list, status filtering, complete, edit, and remove operations.
interfaces.name: Task JSON HTTP API

interfaces.description: The API reads and writes task records through the Postgres connection configured by TODO_DB_CONNECTION.
interfaces.name: Local Postgres

interfaces.description: Docker Compose provides the local Postgres service, readiness check, and persistent volume used by the API and integration tests.
interfaces.name: Docker Compose local runtime

qualityRequirements.statement: The local environment shall be reproducible through Docker Compose with one Postgres service, a persistent volume, readiness checks, bounded connection retry behavior, and documented commands for startup and verification.
Verification shall include pure unit tests and isolated, serial integration tests using real Postgres and real HTTP, covering all six task operations and their principal failure cases.

The implementation shall use Vertical Slice Architecture with operation-specific request handling, validation, persistence interaction, and response mapping, plus only a minimal shared kernel and no generic Controller, Service, or Repository layers.
All client-visible validation and dependency-failure responses shall be sanitized and deterministic, and logs shall redact connection secrets and other sensitive configuration values.
